lines.english: "Ah! This is where Kazusa's concert will take place, right?"
"Yeah… it is."
"This is amazing… How many people can they fit in here? She must truly be above the clouds to play in a venue this big."
"You're right."
Kazusa's concert in Japan is confirmed. January 27th in the Onjuku Art and Culture Hall.
And yesterday, after receiving higher demand than expected, it was confirmed that there is even an additional concert planned a month later.
"I saw the news coverage of her award ceremony earlier. Kazusa has become so beautiful."
"You think so? I don't think she's changed that much."
"That's because she's always been beautiful. But now, I feel she has even exceeded that. It's hard to believe she was our friend once…"
Ever since she found out about this a few days ago, Setsuna has been in high spirits.
Even today, as we walk down the road to the shrine waiting for the new year to come, she's unable to talk about anything else.
Talking about how amazing her classmate was, and about our big moment on the stage back in high school.
…About the homecoming of her friend after five years.
"Hey, Haruki!"
"Eh?"
"Don't attend it. Don't you dare attend her concert, you hear me?"
"How many times do you have to tell me that…? I've already told you I have no intention of going."
And the reaction of the other two is the complete opposite of Setsuna's.
Distancing themselves from the merrymaking Setsuna, and whispering the same thing to me over and over again.
"Setsuna-chan is only pretending. This isn't how she truly feels, I'm sure."
"Don't you go naively buying tickets just because Setsuna says she wants to go."
Not to mention they're assaulting me from both sides.
"I wouldn't be able to get my hands on any tickets even if I tried…"
They started selling the tickets online yesterday.
There were over 2000 tickets. They started selling them at 10 o'clock, and were sold out in less than 30 minutes.

In that time, since so many people were visiting that site, a lot of people couldn't even load the web page before it was all sold out. Now the ticket price on auction sites is already ten times higher than the original price.
"But you have connections, don't you? Your company is sponsoring this concert."
"…I'm amazed you even know that."
Yes, our company, Kaiousha, is listed as one of the sponsors for this grand concert.
To begin with, Touma Youko and Kaiousha… Or rather, her and Ensemble's chief editor have deep connections, so we are involved in practically all of their events.
That's why there's a couple of tickets going around in our editing department, and even people who don't usually listen to classical music are entering a competition to get one.
But I didn't join that competition…
"Also… it's not just about not going to the concert."
"Don't ever meet Touma alone."
"If she contacts you, ignore her."
"That might be cruel to Touma… but it's for the sake of you three."
And so the stereo speakers continue to repeat things around me.
"…I'd never get such a chance in the first place. Who do you think Touma Kazusa is?"
"A former student of Houjou High School."
"A former member of the Light Music Club."
"She's the most popular pianist in Japan. She's being treated like an idol…"
Her skill is certainly part of the reason she's so popular, but the domestic noise being made right now is obviously not just about that.
"Touma Youko's daughter", "The beautiful pianist", "The embodiment of the Japanese dream who made it big overseas."
Just like a certain famous idol that came before her… In fact, people are already looking at her with the same eyes.
"She might return to Japan, but she'll still have her hands full. She won't have any private time to spare…"
"We don't care about her private circumstances… We're asking about you, Haruki."
"…I'm not thinking of meeting her. Not after all this time."
"…Can we trust you on this?"
"Everyone! Hurry up, hurry up! The new year is about to begin!"
"…Of course you can."
I answer with a sigh and lightly wave back at Setsuna, who waves back at me with an exaggerated motion.
Only five minutes left until 2013.
"I want to go to the concert! I hope we can."
"All the tickets for her concert in Tokyo are sold out… Tickets for her additional concert will go on sale at the end of this month."
"I see… Then we better get our hands on them! I'll have to look up the exact date they start selling them."
When the year ended and our shrine visit was over, we said goodbye to Takeya and Io and returned to Minami-Suetsugu, yet Setsuna's spirits were as high as ever.
"Setsuna-chan is only pretending."
After seeing this overly positive attitude, what Takeya said feels more credible. I feel a chill go down my spine.
"Besides, the announcement was far too sudden. If they start selling tickets two days after the announcement, that must mean they've planned for a while now."
"Yeah… they must have planned it."
If they start selling tickets two days after the concert is announced, people will make all sorts of assumptions at this rushed schedule.
Like how they didn't want to let the popularity from their success in the Giovanni International Competition escape them, or like how they were pressured by some big advertising corporation.
Or how they had decided on a concert in Japan a long time ago, but purposefully delayed the announcement to stir people up.
Or how her mother was unsatisfied with the pay, so they were unable to announce it.
But unlike these various speculations, I was supposed to know the real facts.
The most reliable source out there told me that she wasn't going.
That's why I told myself over and over again that our reunion in Strasbourg would be the last time we met.
Kazusa herself said that it was over. She said that the only thing certain is that she's not going to Japan…
But then why…? Why did she turn over what she said herself after a mere two days…?
"…Haruki-kun?"
"It's nothing. Come on, let's go home."
I grab Setsuna's hand and start walking along the road… toward my apartment.
I don't have to think about anything unnecessary. Right now I should only focus on the New Year's Day I will spend with Setsuna.
I'll spend time with Setsuna in my apartment, but not long enough to call it staying over.
Early in the morning, I'll visit the Ogiso household and enjoy New Year's osechi made by Setsuna and her mom.
While being met with her father's awkward expression, I'll enjoy my time there as if I was part of her family.
In the afternoon, we'll visit the shrine with her family. It will be our second time there this year.
Normally, it'd be rude to be imposing on them for the whole day, but in the morning of the second day, Setsuna will come over to my place again.
We'll eat the leftovers of the osechi from the day before, and watch TV together shoulder to shoulder.
Discussing whether we should go buy a mystery package or go out to hang out, but we'll be too lazy to move, so we'll end up spending the entire day in my room.
Like that, lazily, without any change… yet it'll be a period of time that allows me to feel calm, together with Setsuna…
Without worrying about anything else. Merely…
"Hey, Haruki-kun."
"Hm?"
"Do you want to… meet Kazusa?"
"…No, not really."
I didn't want to think about anything else, yet…
Setsuna peers at me thoughtlessly, now that she has finally regained her calm demeanor.
"It's been five years, you know? She's coming back to Japan."
"That has nothing to do with…"
"…It's the first time since that time, you know?"
"Stop it, Setsuna… Why would you say that?"
"I'm sorry…"
"No… It's nothing to apologize about. I should be sorry for putting it that way."
"Haruki-kun…"
"But you know, Setsuna, you've been acting strange today. You seem to be in unusually high spirits today."
"Yes, I am in high spirits. …But only because you're too gloomy, Haruki-kun."
I never realized.
I never realized how those two only went after me and said nothing about Setsuna.
…From the viewpoint of an onlooker, was I the one acting strange?
"So I wanted to know the reason… but I felt like I didn't want to ask somehow, so I started feeling really awkward."
Kazusa isn't what Setsuna was feeling conscious about.
She's feeling conscious about me, who's feeling conscious about Kazusa…
"Hey, Haruki-kun… Kazusa is coming to Japan. She's coming somewhere close to us."
"She'll go straight back to Vienna. The way Touma is right now, she considers Vienna her true hometown."
I'm feeling so conscious about Kazusa that I'm purposefully calling her Touma…
"I won't tell you to not meet Kazusa… I've never asked God for such a thing."
"Setsuna…"
"As long as you remain yourself, Haruki-kun, I'm happy. As you are now."
Setsuna was in high spirits because she was feeling uneasy. All because my uneasiness infected her.
It's because I'm too conscious about Kazusa, because I'm too worried about her.
All because of her… and her whimsicalness.
That's why I have to reassure her. I have to do away with Setsuna's unease.
I…
1. I will never meet Kazusa again.
2. I met Kazusa.
"Even then, I'll never meet Touma again after all."
"Haruki-kun…"
"More importantly, I want to treasure the time I have with you, Setsuna… I can't waste that time meeting her."
It was hardly a satisfactory answer. We both know that.
"Besides… if I did go and meet her and she responded with 'Who the hell are you?' I'd be overcome with shock."
"She'd never say that… Kazusa would never forget you."
That's why Setsuna's unease can't be completely relieved. No matter how much I tell her that she's the only one for me, she won't understand from the bottom of her heart.
That should be obvious… After all, Setsuna isn't a foolish woman who'd let herself be captivated by my improvised lie.
"Regardless, I won't go to meet her. I probably won't see her concert either… I don't want to go, Setsuna."
"I see… That's a shame."
That's just setting the problem aside for later; running away from the reality in front of me. A temporary peace accomplished by not making a resolve.
"Anyway, this conversation is over. Let's go home, Setsuna, to our home."
"…Okay."
I let go of the hand in my grasp and tightly embrace her shoulders once more.
Like this, I can experience her scent, her softness, and her warmth.
I fill my entire consciousness with nothing but Setsuna.
"I look forward to another year together."
"Yes… Happy New Year."
"I won't tell you to not meet Kazusa…"
"As long as you remain yourself, Haruki-kun, I'm happy. As you are now."
Don't say that so easily, Setsuna.
Of course I can't do that…
I…
What am I doing…? Why am I thinking I can cheer Setsuna up right now?
Even though I betrayed Setsuna once again. Even though I've kept silent about something of unparalleled importance…
"You've got it wrong, Setsuna…"
"About what?"
Had I only told her from the start, I wouldn't be tormented by this unease I know the reason for, and Setsuna wouldn't be tormented by this unease she doesn't know the reason for.
"The issue isn't the possibility that I'll meet her in the future."
But it's already too late. An entire week too late.
"The issue is that I've already met her."
We already reunited long ago.
The fact that I've hid this from Setsuna all this time is the final nail in the coffin for the sin I've committed.
"When…? Where…?"
"…In Strasbourg."
With that, it seems that Setsuna understands everything now.
After that…
Just like how people tend to talk at length when confessing to their crimes, I told her about my week-long sin.
I told her about how the job I was suddenly given on the 25th was the widely talked about exclusive interview with the young pianist.
I told her that I didn't know it involved Kazusa until I had already landed.
I told her that Kazusa didn't know it involved me either.
I told her that on the morning of the 25th, after my morning stroll and breakfast with Setsuna, I went to see Kazusa.
I told her that when she was walking the streets alone, I was with Kazusa.
And…
1. That's everything.
2. My reunion with Kazusa was on Christmas Eve.
That's all I decided to admit. That was enough.
"I'm sorry, Setsuna… I'm really sorry."
After all, Setsuna is shocked enough as it is. She's feeling the pain of my betrayal.
There is no need to delve any further. It's nothing she'll forgive just because I tell her regardless.
More importantly, in my eyes, what happened back then…
1. Isn't worth talking about.
2. Isn't something I want to tell anyone.
The wounded tourist happened to be none other than Kazusa.
The reason I couldn't attend Christmas Mass with her was because of Kazusa.
The reason I broke our one-week rule, which we had kept for almost two years, was because of Kazusa.
"I'm sorry, Setsuna… I'm really sorry."
That might have been a superfluous addition. Perhaps nothing more than a meaningless revelation.
On our first ever overseas trip together, I happened to have a reunion with Kazusa. That's all.
Something I never told Setsuna when we were there. Something I kept a secret between Kazusa and me. Nothing more.
But to Setsuna, it's a far too cruel betrayal to say "it's nothing more."
But I tell her anyway. I can't keep it from her.
…Without knowing for whose sake, and without knowing what I'm conveying…
"I… see."
At some point, our hands had separated.
Our course toward my place stops, and we look at each other in silence in the cold breeze.
"So that's what you meant back then… when you were apologizing."
"I'm sorry…"
Setsuna's a smart woman. She's noticed the changes in my demeanor today.
But that's all she's finally come to notice just now.
"Haruki-kun, you were troubled about this all this time. You were unable to tell me, thinking it'd hurt me."
She hadn't noticed… that the change in my demeanor had started as far back as that day.
"I'm a failure as a girlfriend. Thinking to myself that I understand everything about my boyfriend…"
"No, it's not your fault, Setsuna. It's just that I…"
"But even then, even then!"
"I know that it's my fault, and I think it's a given that you couldn't tell me anything, Haruki-kun…"
Setsuna is still feeling tense.
"But I still wish you had told me regardless… I can't stop myself from feeling this way."
…It's just that her tension is now facing the other direction.
"I wanted to see Kazusa too. I wanted to talk to her after all this time."
If I'd told her that Kazusa was nearby back then, I'm sure that Setsuna would've wanted to meet her.
"The three of us could've met up together. We could've talked all night about our memories…"
Had she met Kazusa, there's no doubt she'd have been overcome with emotion. She'd have cried and laughed with a vigor strong enough to never separate them again.
"But I'm the only one who thought of it that way, huh?"
And I'd have looked at the two of them with a smile, but at the same time, I'd have been tortured by regret and a suffocating feeling.
"Perhaps Kazusa doesn't want to meet me. Perhaps you don't want to be seen by me when you're with Kazusa, Haruki-kun."
Kazusa would've talked to Setsuna about their fond memories together, but at times she'd have gone silent with a pained look on her face.
"No, perhaps… I thought so myself too."
And Setsuna…
When she'd said her farewell to Kazusa, and we returned to being just the two of us again, she'd have noticed her own deep wounds and cried without knowing why.
"…I'm sorry. I can't get my thoughts together. I can't talk with you with a smile on my face right now, Haruki-kun."
…Yes, like she is now.
I'm not sure if it's any accurate, but that's how I imagine a reunion between the three of us would look.
"…I'm going home for today."
"Setsuna…"
That's why I couldn't tell Setsuna back then. I knew that no matter when I told her, it'd turn out like this.
"I need to think alone for a while… I'll call you once my thoughts are in order."
All while knowing that the longer I kept the secret, the deeper the wound would be once I did tell her.
"That's why, um…"
"I understand. I'll be waiting… I won't call you until you call me, Setsuna."
"I'm sorry…"
"I should be the one saying… nevermind, good night."
"Good night…"
Setsuna turns around.
Going down the road in the opposite direction to my apartment… toward the station.
"Hey, Haruki-kun! Let's have a good year this year, okay…!?"
But she turns around once more, and forces a smile.
"Yeah… same to you."
Yet at the sight of those eyes on the verge of tears…
I can do nothing but wave my hand back at her.
